finding.text: Every shot is a 404: the only page in the diff (`run-1/readmes-page/`, a one-line `TaskPage`) is not on the main site yet. The branch `task/process-system` is not merged and the site serves the main tree. So "visible on the session page" (requirement 3) has no proof, and none of the page systems can be judged. shots/…/sheet.png, all four widths: "Page Load Error", "404 — nothing matches". Re-shoot after the merge, or shoot it from a served worktree.

Nothing in the diff changes `TaskView` or `TaskPage`. A process shows on the session page only as a plain Task with subtasks. The phase's session, its pulses and its cost (`measure` lines) are written to the file but not drawn anywhere. requirements.md §3 asks only for "whatever shows today", so this is a note, not a fix.

process.md's own "Still open" line: the answer to the creating `item` call carries the instructions for the parent's class, not for the new process. That is a small trap for the next agent that creates a process.

"Investigate" exists as its own definition. It does not run as build's first phase yet: phases cannot nest, and parallel scouts are not built. process.md lists both under ⬜ Next, so this is an honest gap, not a hidden one.

The daily respawn will probably never fire for the real architect. `held()` treats any `state === "stopped"` as "stopped on purpose" (Servex/agents/Respawn.js:101), but the Lifecycle reaper stops idle agents whose task has landed with no `by` (Servex/Lifecycle.js:277, 310). The process-system task already reads `complete` (process.md Status), and `mastermind-system-architect` is not in the reaper's standing-agent list (Lifecycle.js:245). So after a quiet day the architect is reaped, and Respawn then skips it forever. Fix: test `row.stopped_by` alone (a reaped row has none), or add the id to the reaper's exemption list, and add a test for "reaped idle, a day old → respawned".

Requirement 2 says "completion is automatic", but process.md:143 records a known break: a landed task that gets new open children still reads `complete`. This diff now makes that case common, because requests add tasks to other agents' task logs (page_tools.js:225–249). A request added to a landed task stays invisible to completion. Adding an open child to a complete task should reopen it, in Task's replay, with a test.

Most of this diff is outside requirements.md: the session menu and settings, Respawn, requests as logged items, the `design` process, the one-stream design and the docs-vs-logs rule. Each follows a later owner dictation. The brief's own deliverables (Process, ProcessRunner, process.md, run 1, the "document per prompt" rule in mastermind.md:20) landed in earlier commits (b8d7e49f9, 60808be61). Splitting this into separate branches would make each merge easier to judge.

The session menu changes a page (core/Page/Columns.js:48, Page.css:661, AISessionDetail.js:116), but no shot shows it. The only shots in this folder are the 404s from the earlier review (review/report.md finding 1). The button, its popover and `/settings/` need one shot each at 400 and 1200 from a served worktree before the merge.

Respawn's list is a hard-coded static holding one dated folder path (Respawn.js:74–78). A simpler way: a `fresh_daily: true` flag on the spawn spec or registry row, read by the tick. Then the next standing agent needs no code edit, and the path is not copied into a second place.

SessionSettings saves model, effort and notify, but nothing reads them yet (core/Session/doc/menu.md, "Not built yet"). This is stated honestly. Still, an owner who sets "Model: Opus" today gets no effect and no warning on the form. Add one line on the Settings page saying so.

Any caller that is not the log's own agent counts as an asker (page_tools.js:225), including `owner` from the browser and a parent adding steps to its minion's task. Each of those adds now sends the receiver a chat notice. That is probably intended, but messaging.md:164 should say that parent-to-child adds count too.
The `hooks` line in page_tools.js:642 now holds two trailing `//` comments one after the other, and the second one is cut off from its key. Put each comment on its own key.
